LIMITED PARTNER CONTROL SAFE HARBOR — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Casey Alex · Acme Ventures, LP

IDENTIFICATION
This information sheet concerns Casey Alex, a limited partner of Acme Ventures, LP, a California limited partnership whose general partner is Jordan Lee. It addresses the statutory rule under which a limited partner may engage in certain activities without being treated, for liability purposes, as having "participate[d] in the control of the business" of the limited partnership.

THE SAFE-HARBOR RULE FOR LIMITED PARTNER CONDUCT
California's limited partnership statute qualifies the general "participating in control" liability test with a safe harbor: a limited partner does not participate in the control of the business, within the meaning of the general liability rule, solely by doing, attempting to do, or having the right or power to do one or more of thirteen enumerated things. The statute separately states that this enumeration does not mean that other conduct, or the possession or exercise of other powers, by a limited partner automatically counts as participating in control — the list defines what is safe, not what is unsafe.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "A limited partner does not participate in the control of the business within the meaning of subdivision (a) solely by doing, attempting to do, or having the right or power to do, one or more of the following:"
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 15903.03 (California Legislative Information text), California Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act of 2008, safe-harbor introductory clause (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=15903.03.)
  "(c) The enumeration in subdivision (b) does not mean that any other conduct or the possession or exercise of any other power by a limited partner constitutes participation by the limited partner in the control of the business of the limited partnership."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 15903.03 (California Legislative Information text), California Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act of 2008, enumeration is not exhaustive of what constitutes control (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=15903.03.)
  Known gap: This clause states only the introductory clause of Cal. Corp. Code § 15903.03(b) and all of subdivision (c). It does not state the underlying “participates in the control of the business” liability rule itself (Cal. Corp. Code § 15903.03(a)), which this project's California Limited Partnership Formation Information Sheet addresses in a separate clause (id: lpform_lp_liability_shield) citing the same statute's subdivision (a). The thirteen specific enumerated activities referenced here are stated individually in the companion clauses of this document, not in this clause. This clause does not state what conduct, beyond the enumerated list, a court has found does or does not amount to participation in control — subdivision (c) leaves that question open, and no case law was independently researched for this clause.

SAFE HARBOR: HOLDING A RELATED ROLE OR TRANSACTING BUSINESS
Among the activities the statute places inside the safe harbor is holding certain roles connected to the limited partnership or its general partner. The statute lists, as things that alone do not amount to participating in control: being an independent contractor for, an agent or employee of, or a party transacting business with, the limited partnership or a general partner; being an officer, director, or shareholder of a corporate general partner; being a member, manager, or officer of an LLC general partner; being a limited partner of a partnership that is itself a general partner; being a trustee, administrator, executor, custodian, or other fiduciary or beneficiary of an estate or trust that is a general partner; and being a trustee, officer, adviser, shareholder, or beneficiary of a business trust that is a general partner.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "(1) Being any of the following:(A) An independent contractor for, an agent or employee of, or transacting business with, the limited partnership or a general partner of the limited partnership.(B) An officer, director, or shareholder of a corporate general partner of the limited partnership.(C) A member, manager, or officer of a limited liability company that is a general partner of the limited partnership.(D) A limited partner of a partnership that is a general partner of the limited partnership.(E) A trustee, administrator, executor, custodian, or other fiduciary or beneficiary of an estate or trust that is a general partner.(F) A trustee, officer, adviser, shareholder, or beneficiary of a business trust that is a general partner."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 15903.03 (California Legislative Information text), California Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act of 2008, roles connected to the limited partnership or a general partner (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=15903.03.)
  Known gap: This states only Cal. Corp. Code § 15903.03(b)(1)(A)-(F). It does not address whether a specific person's actual role or business dealings fall within one of these six listed categories, nor does it address what other conduct that same person might separately engage in that could fall outside the safe harbor — the safe harbor protects only the listed status or activity itself, not necessarily every other thing the same person does. Cal. Corp. Code § 15903.03(b)(1) was not cross-checked against the parallel Delaware or other-state limited partnership statutes on which it is modeled.

SAFE HARBOR: CONSULTING, ADVISING, AND EXTENDING OR RECEIVING CREDIT
The statute also places two financial and advisory activities inside the safe harbor. First, consulting with and advising a general partner regarding the business of the limited partnership does not, by itself, amount to participating in control. Second, a list of credit-related dealings with the limited partnership or a general partner — acting as surety, guaranteeing specific debts, providing collateral, borrowing money, or lending money — likewise does not, by itself, amount to participating in control.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "(2) Consulting with and advising a general partner with respect to the business of the limited partnership."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 15903.03 (California Legislative Information text), California Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act of 2008, consulting with and advising a general partner (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=15903.03.)
  "(3) Acting as surety for the limited partnership or for a general partner, guaranteeing one or more specific debts of the limited partnership, providing collateral for the limited partnership or general partner, borrowing money from the limited partnership or a general partner, or lending money to the limited partnership or a general partner."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 15903.03 (California Legislative Information text), California Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act of 2008, suretyship, guaranty, collateral, and lending or borrowing (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=15903.03.)
  Known gap: This states only Cal. Corp. Code § 15903.03(b)(2) and (b)(3). It does not address how much consulting or advising, or how large or frequent a credit transaction, might combine with other conduct outside this safe harbor to support a finding of control in a specific case — the statute does not quantify a limit, and no case law applying these paragraphs was independently researched for this clause.

SAFE HARBOR: VOTING, MEETINGS, AND APPROVAL COMMITTEES
The statute places core governance participation inside the safe harbor as well. Approving or disapproving an amendment to the partnership agreement does not, by itself, amount to participating in control. Voting on, proposing, or calling a meeting of the partners does not, by itself, amount to participating in control. Serving on a committee of the limited partnership or the limited partners for the purpose of approving actions of the general partner does not, by itself, amount to participating in control. And calling, requesting, attending, or participating at any meeting of the partners or the limited partners does not, by itself, amount to participating in control.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "(4) Approving or disapproving an amendment to the partnership agreement."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 15903.03 (California Legislative Information text), California Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act of 2008, approving or disapproving a partnership agreement amendment (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=15903.03.)
  "(5) Voting on, proposing, or calling a meeting of the partners."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 15903.03 (California Legislative Information text), California Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act of 2008, voting on, proposing, or calling a partner meeting (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=15903.03.)
  "(9) Serving on a committee of the limited partnership or the limited partners for the purpose of approving actions of the general partner."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 15903.03 (California Legislative Information text), California Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act of 2008, serving on a committee that approves general partner actions (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=15903.03.)
  "(10) Calling, requesting, attending, or participating at any meeting of the partners or the limited partners."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 15903.03 (California Legislative Information text), California Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act of 2008, calling, requesting, attending, or participating at a meeting (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=15903.03.)
  Known gap: This states only Cal. Corp. Code § 15903.03(b)(4), (b)(5), (b)(9), and (b)(10). It does not address what a limited partner does or says at such a meeting, vote, or committee session beyond the acts of attending, voting, proposing, calling, or serving — conduct at a meeting that goes beyond these listed acts is not addressed by this clause. It also does not address any quorum, notice, or voting-threshold rules that might separately govern how partnership-agreement amendments or partner meetings are conducted, which were not independently researched for this clause.

SAFE HARBOR: WINDING UP AND CERTAIN SECRETARY OF STATE FILINGS
The statute places two administrative and wind-down activities inside the safe harbor. Winding up the limited partnership under the statute's own winding-up provision does not, by itself, amount to participating in control. Executing and filing a certificate under the statute's certificate-of-limited-partnership provision, a certificate of withdrawal under a specified paragraph of the statute's certificate-of-limited-partnership-amendment provision, or a certificate of cancellation under another specified paragraph of that same provision, likewise does not, by itself, amount to participating in control.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "(6) Winding up the partnership pursuant to Section 15908.03."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 15903.03 (California Legislative Information text), California Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act of 2008, winding up the partnership (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=15903.03.)
  "(7) Executing and filing a certificate pursuant to Section 15902.05, a certificate of withdrawal pursuant to paragraph (4) of subdivision (a) of Section 15902.04, or a certificate of cancellation of the certificate of limited partnership pursuant to paragraph (6) of subdivision (a) of Section 15902.04."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 15903.03 (California Legislative Information text), California Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act of 2008, executing and filing certain certificates (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=15903.03.)
  Known gap: This states only Cal. Corp. Code § 15903.03(b)(6) and (b)(7). The cross-referenced statutes it names — Cal. Corp. Code §§ 15908.03 (winding up), 15902.05 (certificate contents), and 15902.04(a)(4) and (a)(6) (withdrawal and cancellation certificates) — were not independently fetched or verified for this clause; their own text, and any conditions those statutes place on when a limited partner may wind up the partnership or execute these filings, are outside what this clause states.

SAFE HARBOR: AUDIT OVERSIGHT, DERIVATIVE ACTIONS, RELATED-ENTITY ROLES, AND THE CATCH-ALL
The statute places four further categories inside the safe harbor. Serving on an audit committee, or a committee performing audit-committee functions, does not, by itself, amount to participating in control. Taking any action required or permitted by law to bring, pursue, settle, or terminate a derivative action on the limited partnership's behalf does not, by itself, amount to participating in control. Serving on the board or a committee of, consulting with or advising, acting as an officer, director, stockholder, partner, member, manager, agent, or employee of, or acting as a fiduciary for, any entity in which the limited partnership itself holds an interest, does not, by itself, amount to participating in control. And, as a residual catch-all, exercising any right or power the statute permits to limited partners that is not specifically listed in the enumeration does not, by itself, amount to participating in control.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "(8) Serving on an audit committee or committee performing the functions of an audit committee."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 15903.03 (California Legislative Information text), California Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act of 2008, audit committee service (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=15903.03.)
  "(11) Taking any action required or permitted by law to bring, pursue, settle, or terminate a derivative action on behalf of the limited partnership."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 15903.03 (California Legislative Information text), California Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act of 2008, derivative action conduct (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=15903.03.)
  "(12) Serving on the board of directors or a committee of, consulting with or advising, being or acting as an officer, director, stockholder, partner, member, manager, agent, or employee of, or being or acting as a fiduciary for, any person in which the limited partnership has an interest."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 15903.03 (California Legislative Information text), California Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act of 2008, roles in an entity in which the limited partnership has an interest (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=15903.03.)
  "(13) Exercising any right or power permitted to limited partners under this chapter and not specifically enumerated in this subdivision."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 15903.03 (California Legislative Information text), California Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act of 2008, residual catch-all for unenumerated statutory rights or powers (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=15903.03.)
  Known gap: This states only Cal. Corp. Code § 15903.03(b)(8), (b)(11), (b)(12), and (b)(13). The catch-all in paragraph (13) reaches only rights or powers the statute itself permits to limited partners — it does not extend the safe harbor to conduct that is not otherwise a right or power granted by the Uniform Limited Partnership Act of 2008, and this clause does not attempt to enumerate what those other statutory rights or powers are. What qualifies as a derivative action, or as the requirements for bringing one, is governed by other statutory and procedural rules not addressed by this clause.

A SEPARATE PROTECTION FOR A GOOD-FAITH BUT MISTAKEN LIMITED PARTNER
California's limited partnership statute separately protects a person who invests in a business enterprise erroneously but in good faith believing they have become a limited partner. Such a person is not liable for the enterprise's obligations by reason of making the investment, receiving distributions, or exercising rights of or appropriate to a limited partner, if, on discovering the mistake, the person either causes an appropriate certificate of limited partnership, amendment, or certificate of correction to be filed with the Secretary of State, or withdraws from future participation by filing a certificate of withdrawal on the form the Secretary of State prescribes. That protection has its own limit: the same person remains liable to the same extent as a general partner to a third party who, before the correcting or withdrawal filing is made, enters into a transaction with the enterprise in the good-faith belief that the person is a general partner.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "(a) Except as otherwise provided in subdivision (b), a person that makes an investment in a business enterprise and erroneously but in good faith believes that the person has become a limited partner in the enterprise is not liable for the enterprise’s obligations by reason of making the investment, receiving distributions from the enterprise, or exercising any rights of or appropriate to a limited partner, if, on ascertaining the mistake, the person:"
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 15903.06 (California Legislative Information text), California Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act of 2008, protection for a good-faith erroneous investor who cures the mistake (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=15903.06.)
  "(1) causes an appropriate certificate of limited partnership, amendment, or certificate of correction to be signed and delivered to the Secretary of State for filing; or"
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 15903.06 (California Legislative Information text), California Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act of 2008, curing by a correcting Secretary of State filing (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=15903.06.)
  "(2) withdraws from future participation as an owner in the enterprise by signing and delivering to and on a form prescribed by the Secretary of State for filing a certificate of withdrawal containing the name of the limited partnership and the Secretary of State’s file number of the limited partnership under this section."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 15903.06 (California Legislative Information text), California Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act of 2008, curing by a certificate of withdrawal (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=15903.06.)
  "(b) A person that makes an investment described in subdivision (a) is liable to the same extent as a general partner to any third party that enters into a transaction with the enterprise, believing in good faith that the person is a general partner, before the Secretary of State files a certificate of withdrawal, certificate of limited partnership, amendment, or certificate of correction to show that the person is not a general partner."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 15903.06 (California Legislative Information text), California Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act of 2008, liability to a third party who relied before the correcting filing (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=15903.06.)
  Known gap: This states only Cal. Corp. Code § 15903.06(a) and (b). It does not address subdivision (c)'s separate rule permitting withdrawal, notwithstanding a contrary agreement with co-owners, for a person who diligently but unsuccessfully attempts in good faith to file a correcting certificate — that rule is addressed in a separate companion clause of this document. This clause does not state what facts are sufficient to show a person's belief that they had become a limited partner was held erroneously but in good faith, nor whether any specific investor's belief or conduct meets that standard; that is a fact-specific inquiry this clause does not resolve.

THE RIGHT TO WITHDRAW WHEN A DILIGENT GOOD-FAITH CORRECTION EFFORT FAILS
The statute adds a further rule for the good-faith erroneous investor described elsewhere in this document: if that person makes a diligent, good-faith effort to file the correcting certificate described in the statute but is unable to cause it to be signed and delivered to the Secretary of State for filing, the person still has the right to withdraw from the enterprise by filing a certificate of withdrawal — and the statute states that this withdrawal right exists even if the withdrawal would otherwise breach an agreement with others who are or have agreed to become co-owners of the enterprise.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "(c) If a person makes a diligent effort in good faith to comply with paragraph (1) of subdivision (a) and is unable"
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 15903.06 (California Legislative Information text), California Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act of 2008, diligent good-faith effort that fails to secure a correcting certificate (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=15903.06.)
  "to cause the appropriate certificate of limited partnership, amendment, or certificate of correction to be signed and delivered to the Secretary of State for filing, the person has the right to withdraw from the enterprise pursuant to paragraph (2) of subdivision (a) even if the withdrawal would otherwise breach an agreement with others that are or have agreed to become co-owners of the enterprise."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 15903.06 (California Legislative Information text), California Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act of 2008, withdrawal permitted despite a contrary co-owner agreement (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=15903.06.)
  Known gap: This states only Cal. Corp. Code § 15903.06(c). It does not define what constitutes a “diligent effort in good faith” for purposes of this subdivision, nor does it address any liability the withdrawing person might otherwise have already incurred under subdivision (b) toward a third party who relied on the person's apparent status before the withdrawal certificate was filed. Whether a specific person's effort to obtain a correcting signature was sufficiently diligent is a fact-specific question this clause does not resolve.

PREPARATION AND SIGNATURE BLOCK
This information sheet regarding Casey Alex's status as a limited partner of Acme Ventures, LP was prepared by Jordan Lee.

Executed on September 6, 2026 at Sacramento, California.

Signature of Jordan Lee: ☐ _________________________

expectedJSON.gap: This states only Cal. Corp. Code § 15903.03(b)(8), (b)(11), (b)(12), and (b)(13). The catch-all in paragraph (13) reaches only rights or powers the statute itself permits to limited partners — it does not extend the safe harbor to conduct that is not otherwise a right or power granted by the Uniform Limited Partnership Act of 2008, and this clause does not attempt to enumerate what those other statutory rights or powers are. What qualifies as a derivative action, or as the requirements for bringing one, is governed by other statutory and procedural rules not addressed by this clause.

expectedJSON.body: California's limited partnership statute separately protects a person who invests in a business enterprise erroneously but in good faith believing they have become a limited partner. Such a person is not liable for the enterprise's obligations by reason of making the investment, receiving distributions, or exercising rights of or appropriate to a limited partner, if, on discovering the mistake, the person either causes an appropriate certificate of limited partnership, amendment, or certificate of correction to be filed with the Secretary of State, or withdraws from future participation by filing a certificate of withdrawal on the form the Secretary of State prescribes. That protection has its own limit: the same person remains liable to the same extent as a general partner to a third party who, before the correcting or withdrawal filing is made, enters into a transaction with the enterprise in the good-faith belief that the person is a general partner.

citations.case: Cal. Corp. Code § 15903.06 (California Legislative Information text)
citations.cite: California Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act of 2008, protection for a good-faith erroneous investor who cures the mistake
citations.quote: (a) Except as otherwise provided in subdivision (b), a person that makes an investment in a business enterprise and erroneously but in good faith believes that the person has become a limited partner in the enterprise is not liable for the enterprise’s obligations by reason of making the investment, receiving distributions from the enterprise, or exercising any rights of or appropriate to a limited partner, if, on ascertaining the mistake, the person:

citations.case: Cal. Corp. Code § 15903.06 (California Legislative Information text)
citations.cite: California Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act of 2008, curing by a correcting Secretary of State filing
citations.quote: (1) causes an appropriate certificate of limited partnership, amendment, or certificate of correction to be signed and delivered to the Secretary of State for filing; or

citations.case: Cal. Corp. Code § 15903.06 (California Legislative Information text)
citations.cite: California Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act of 2008, curing by a certificate of withdrawal
citations.quote: (2) withdraws from future participation as an owner in the enterprise by signing and delivering to and on a form prescribed by the Secretary of State for filing a certificate of withdrawal containing the name of the limited partnership and the Secretary of State’s file number of the limited partnership under this section.

citations.case: Cal. Corp. Code § 15903.06 (California Legislative Information text)
citations.cite: California Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act of 2008, liability to a third party who relied before the correcting filing
citations.quote: (b) A person that makes an investment described in subdivision (a) is liable to the same extent as a general partner to any third party that enters into a transaction with the enterprise, believing in good faith that the person is a general partner, before the Secretary of State files a certificate of withdrawal, certificate of limited partnership, amendment, or certificate of correction to show that the person is not a general partner.

expectedJSON.gap: This states only Cal. Corp. Code § 15903.06(a) and (b). It does not address subdivision (c)'s separate rule permitting withdrawal, notwithstanding a contrary agreement with co-owners, for a person who diligently but unsuccessfully attempts in good faith to file a correcting certificate — that rule is addressed in a separate companion clause of this document. This clause does not state what facts are sufficient to show a person's belief that they had become a limited partner was held erroneously but in good faith, nor whether any specific investor's belief or conduct meets that standard; that is a fact-specific inquiry this clause does not resolve.

expectedJSON.body: The statute adds a further rule for the good-faith erroneous investor described elsewhere in this document: if that person makes a diligent, good-faith effort to file the correcting certificate described in the statute but is unable to cause it to be signed and delivered to the Secretary of State for filing, the person still has the right to withdraw from the enterprise by filing a certificate of withdrawal — and the statute states that this withdrawal right exists even if the withdrawal would otherwise breach an agreement with others who are or have agreed to become co-owners of the enterprise.

citations.cite: California Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act of 2008, diligent good-faith effort that fails to secure a correcting certificate
citations.quote: (c) If a person makes a diligent effort in good faith to comply with paragraph (1) of subdivision (a) and is unable

citations.case: Cal. Corp. Code § 15903.06 (California Legislative Information text)
citations.cite: California Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act of 2008, withdrawal permitted despite a contrary co-owner agreement
citations.quote: to cause the appropriate certificate of limited partnership, amendment, or certificate of correction to be signed and delivered to the Secretary of State for filing, the person has the right to withdraw from the enterprise pursuant to paragraph (2) of subdivision (a) even if the withdrawal would otherwise breach an agreement with others that are or have agreed to become co-owners of the enterprise.

expectedJSON.gap: This states only Cal. Corp. Code § 15903.06(c). It does not define what constitutes a “diligent effort in good faith” for purposes of this subdivision, nor does it address any liability the withdrawing person might otherwise have already incurred under subdivision (b) toward a third party who relied on the person's apparent status before the withdrawal certificate was filed. Whether a specific person's effort to obtain a correcting signature was sufficiently diligent is a fact-specific question this clause does not resolve.
